newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London cautiously higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London cautiously higher.

text.p: U.S. shares were generally firmer but European investors remained nervous following Wall Street's sharp declines last week, dealers here said.
"We're seeing a slight rebound but volumes are nothing much," one dealer said. "No one is rushing in to snap up bargains just yet. This market is tricky and could easily come off again."

The Dow Industrials Average fell 55 points on Friday and ended the week 140 points lower. Dealers here expect a solid start for the Dow on Monday but aren't convinced a significant rally is on the cards.

"The only thing you can say with any certainty is that this market will either fall sharply or rise sharply. We'll have a good open today but any gains could be erased with a sell-off in the final 30 minutes," another dealer said.
Boeing was down $1/2 at $95-1/8 after press reports that British Airways had shelved plans to be a launch customer for the aircraft manufacturer's super-747 jumbo jet.
Elsewhere, General Motors, which dropped $2-3/8 on Friday was $1/4 higher at $56-3/4.
Microsoft, which had a two-for-one share split on Monday, was up $1/2 at $76-1/2.
The software company also plans to increase spending for basic research by 300 percent, according to Monday's edition of the New York Times newspaper.
Amongst other high-techs, Intel was up $3/8 at $126 and Texas Instruments rose $1/4 at $64-1/4.
The March U.S. T-bond futures contract was up 16/32 at 114-11/32 by 1045GMT.
